small_guidance:
- Add wider HW tiles (BLOCK_HW=512) and try BLOCK_OC=64/BLOCK_HW=256 with num_warps=8, num_stages=3/4 — with C_IN=8, KH=KW=3 the K-loop has only 72 iters, so larger output tiles amortize the bias/Mish epilogue and weight loads better.
- Hoist weight loads: load the full `(BLOCK_OC, C_IN*KH*KW)` weight tile once into registers/SMEM outside the spatial loops (it's only 64×72=4608 floats for the full OC), then reuse across all HW iterations; current code reloads `w_val` inside the kh/kw/ic triple loop.
- Use vectorized contiguous loads along W: have each program own a contiguous row segment (BLOCK_W along W_OUT, BLOCK_H along H_OUT) instead of a flat HW range, so `ih*W_IN+iw` loads coalesce and you can share `x_val` across kw with a shift.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an implicit-GEMM with M=C_OUT, N=N*H_OUT*W_OUT (or tiled over N and a 2D spatial tile), K=C_IN*KH*KW=72. Use `tl.dot` on BLOCK_M×BLOCK_K @ BLOCK_K×BLOCK_N tiles (pad K to 128) — this gets you tensor-core throughput instead of the current scalar FMA accumulation, which is the main reason a 13.9 ms kernel is losing to 7.3 ms cuDNN.
- Adopt NHWC (channels-last) layout for the input and output so the K-reduction (C_IN×KH×KW) is contiguous; do a one-time layout transform on the weight at init and on the input in forward (or fuse the transpose into the load pattern). This lets the GEMM-K loads coalesce and enables `tl.dot`.
- Fuse bias-subtract-Mish strictly in the epilogue on the accumulator (already done) and consider a persistent-CTA scheme where each program iterates over multiple (N, spatial-tile) pairs to amortize weight-tile loads across the batch — N=128 gives lots of reuse of the same 64×72 weight tile.
